layout.description: Reread a text or test yourself? In a published experiment with 120 students, rereading was ahead after five minutes, testing after two days and after one week. Setup, measure, result, limits and state of research, retold from the original study. Plus a small test for you, with a counting rule.

beats.spoken: Reread a text, or test yourself? An experiment with one hundred twenty students compared exactly that. After five minutes, rereading was ahead. After one week, it was not.

data.question: Reread or test yourself?
data.cite: Roediger & Karpicke 2006 · Psychol. Sci. 17(3) · Exp. 1, p. 250

beats.spoken: Here is how it worked. Everyone read two short science texts, seven minutes each. They read one text a second time. For the other, they wrote down everything they remembered, with no feedback. A third took the final test after five minutes, a third after two days, a third after one week.

data.headline: How it worked
data.cite: Roediger & Karpicke 2006 · Psychol. Sci. 17(3) · Exp. 1, p. 250

beats.spoken: The measure was what came back. Each text was split into thirty idea units. Every unit written down correctly scored one point.

data.headline: Measured: what came back

sample.text: First recall in the study: avg 20.9 of 30

data.cite: Roediger & Karpicke 2006 · Psychol. Sci. 17(3) · Exp. 1, p. 250

beats.spoken: After five minutes: rereading eighty-one percent, testing seventy-five. After two days it flips, fifty-four versus sixty-eight. After one week, forty-two versus fifty-six.

data.headline: Result
data.cite: Roediger & Karpicke 2006 · Psychol. Sci. 17(3) · Exp. 1, p. 251

beats.spoken: The limits: students at one university, two texts, one lab. But the finding does not stand alone. A meta-analysis from twenty seventeen found testing more effective than rereading across many studies.

evidence.cite: Adesope, Trevisan & Sundararajan, Rev. Educ. Res.
Dunlosky et al., Psychol. Sci. Public Interest

data.cite: Adesope et al. 2017 · Dunlosky et al. 2013

beats.spoken: Your test: two sections. Reread one, close the book on the other and write down what you know. After a week, write down both and count. It proves nothing, but you will see for yourself. More real experiments: follow Gritwerk.

data.title: Your test · n = 1

steps.text: Pick two sections of equal length
A: reread. B: close the book, write it down

caveat.text: n = 1 shows you something, proves nothing
